slides.headline: October 18, 1861: Delhi's first-ever police complaint was written down - in Urdu and Persian.
Sabzi Mandi Police Station registered Delhi's first First Information Report
slides.body: A resident named Maiuddin reported the theft of household items - women's clothing, a hookah, cooking pots, a bowl - valued at about 45 annas, roughly Rs 2.80 at the time.

slides.headline: It came just months after the Police Act of 1861 created the modern Indian police force.
slides.body: Written partly in Urdu and partly in Persian - the official languages of court and police records at the time - a copy still survives today, preserved at the Delhi Police Museum.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs institutions that keep records, not just laws.
slides.body: A theft worth less than three rupees became the starting point for a record-keeping system that, over 165 years later, still structures how every crime in India gets reported and tracked.
